summary:
Outcome. Branch stage1c-m1-switches-2 in the worktree /Users/acoerduek/Documents/workspace/cuopt/.claude/worktrees/wf_e509c798-6d7-1 holds two new commits on the base fa8430e24: d15144a21 (engine options, counters, tools, tests, wrong engines) and 55b639503 (the stored runs of every option value and one more test). The saved commit ec7a30dcf is not an ancestor. Every choice of the singleton-column rules that the task lists now has an engine option whose default is the rule as it was: 12 options with 21 other values. Six values named in the register are not built, each with its reason (the test of the bound ahead only is not valid; the model that breaks it is in the header).

What I took over and what I changed. I took the first agent's state, read its whole diff against Parts A to E, and reran everything from my own commit: none of its runs is used in this report. My three tables of Part E are equal, line by line, to the tables it left. I changed four things in its source: (1) with singleton_order single_pass a call ended after any pass; a pass without a reduction can still list columns, so a presolve could claim a fixed point with a list left. The call now ends only after a pass with a reduction (test added; it fails with the old form). (2) Counting was made cheaper (the scan for integral ratios is one scan of a row that has a candidate, two counters are sums taken at the end of a call). (3) The wrong engine sw_descending_coefficient was caught by no check; a test with two different coefficients catches it now. (4) Two header contracts were completed (why the inequality pivot needs both ends; what "off" means against HiGHS). I added tools/reduce_summary.py and the reduced result files.

Verified, all on the Mac, at most 3 processes of mine. Tests: 500 pass in the assertion and in the release build, built from the committed tree. Identity at the defaults against the base: 0 differences on the 240 local dumps in the three stored modes, on the 17 local dumps, and on 2,016,000 random models per mode and build with the record stack hashed field by field. Campaign with the option drawing: 30,240,000 models in the release build and 15,120,000 in the assertion build (10,080,000 and 5,040,000 for each of no profile option, --singletons, --columns): no failure except one in the release run with --columns that I could not reproduce in four reruns of the same part, a rerun of the whole run, and the model alone (see unsure). Wrong engines: all 113 apply and are caught; the 99 old ones have the campaign counts of the stored table of the base commit. Structure check on the 240 and structure and crush check with points on the 17: pass for all 31 option settings. Time at the defaults: +0.7% and +0.2% in two runs, two copies of one binary differ by 0.2%.

Numbers that an owner's decision can use now (no recommendation): integer pivot columns of the inequality pivot off (AS-339) makes 10 of the 240 instances larger and gives exactly the size of the HiGHS reference m1_a on 8 of them; 271 of the 2,685 findings of the rule are integer columns. The two projections on in primal-only mode (AS-004) give 1.0017 / 1.0005 / 1.0073 in nonzeros / rows / columns over 237 instances, 22 smaller, none larger, and pass the crush check. The growth ratio over continuous columns only (AS-318) gives 1.0003 / 1.0005 / 1.0003, 6 instances smaller. 50,771 zero-cost integer singleton columns are left in rows that are integral for them (AS-029 asked for this count; the rule that would take them is not built).

Not done: nothing ran with a solver, on the node (no remote command was allowed, so the two slots were not used), or on the 40 testbed instances; five option values are never reached by the campaign generator and rest on unit tests and the dump checks; AddressSanitizer hangs on this machine; no HISTORY.md entry and no register update were written (task rules).

switches.choice: The zero-cost singleton rule [R3] and the forcing column [R4] are off in primal-only mode although both are exact projections.
switches.option: options_t::primal_projections, default false (as today), other value true; tool flag --primal-projections. It acts only together with --primal-only.
switches.validity: Both rules are exact projections of the feasible set onto the columns that stay, and the removed columns cost nothing. So every feasible point crushes, by dropping the columns, to a feasible point of the reduced model with the same objective value, and result_t::dual_findings stays 0: that is what primal-only mode promises. What they read of a cost and of the locks is no optimality argument: the cost must be exactly zero, and the lock counts of a forcing column only say that each of its rows has one finite side and holds the column from the same end. What the mode loses: crush is no longer one to one, so a postsolved point can differ from the crushed one in the columns of interval and forcing records and in columns restored from them. Clause 5 of the crush check already exempts exactly these columns and allows a defined column what its saved columns moved by; I checked that this is enough in the check tool (below) and on generated models. The campaign's own crush test has no round trip; it tests that every feasible point crushes to a feasible point of equal objective, which holds.
switches.covered_by: Unit tests switches_primal_projections_which_reductions, _zero_cost, _forcing_column, _presolve, and switches_primal_projections_checks_on_generated_models (4,000 generated models in primal-only mode with the option: structure check silent, crush check with clause 5 on more than 2,000 points with more than 200 exempt columns). Campaign value primal_projections: release 909,564 alone, 5,242 changed, 2,727,996 among several; assertion build 454,272 / 2,558 / 1,359,816 (it changes a result only on seeds whose option variant is primal-only). Wrong engine sw_primal_dual (the dual pivot also runs with the option): campaign with --switches oracle 581 and structure check 584 of 1,440,000 models, and 2 unit tests. Check tool on the 17 local dumps with stored points, primal-only mode with the option: the round trip of the crush check passes on all 13 instances that have usable points (344 points, 336 exempt columns, all on unitcal_7) and is skipped on the 4 without points; on the 240 the structure check of that mode passes with 13,213 defined, 117 forcing and 17,901 interval records.
switches.measured: 240 local dumps, primal-only mode. With the option the mode makes 36,416 zero-cost and 117 forcing-column findings. Fixed-point flags 233 with both values. Against m1_a: 0.9557 / 0.9621 / 0.9408 with the option, 0.9540 / 0.9616 / 0.9340 without. These are the figures of the M1 worth report. In default mode the option does nothing.
switches.where: gpu_presolve/include/gprs/presolve.hpp:243 (option and contract) and :323 (sub_rule_active, which reads it); gpu_presolve/check/structure_check.hpp:2126 (the check takes the options of the presolve).

switches.choice: The growth ratio of a free singleton column reads the largest coefficient of every other free column of the pivot row, and applies to integer pivot columns too.
switches.option: options_t::growth_ratio, default growth_ratio_t::all_columns (as today), other values continuous_columns and integer_pivot_exempt; tool flag --growth-ratio <all|continuous|integer-exempt>. It stands next to pivot_growth_limit and saved_row_factor, which are unchanged.
switches.validity: The limit is a guard on how much a restored value can multiply a deviation of the reduced point; no reduction depends on it for exact points. An integer column brings no deviation: postsolve() rounds the integer columns of the reduced point before any undo (src/postsolve.cpp:454), and a rounded value lies inside its integral bounds when the point is within the tolerance. So reading continuous columns only is as safe as the form of today for one link. An integer pivot column has only integer columns next to it (the integrality condition is tested before), and its own value is rounded, so exempting it is the same argument. The factor that a substitution passes on to the columns of its saved row is unchanged in every form.
switches.covered_by: Unit tests switches_growth_ratio_of_a_continuous_column and switches_growth_ratio_of_an_integer_column (the three forms on a row with ratio 2000). switches.choice: The free singleton column on an inequality tests the bound behind its move as well as the one ahead.
switches.validity: Testing the bound ahead only is not valid, and the sentence of the design and of the register that the exchange needs only the bound ahead is wrong for the reduction as built. The exchange shows that an optimal point has the row tight. It does not allow the row to leave: the row and the bound behind the move together restrict the other columns, and that restriction leaves with the row. Smallest model: min -x - 3 y with x + y <= 5 and x, y in [0, 10], continuous or integer. The optimum is -15 at (0, 5). The cost moves x up, the row implies the bound ahead (x <= 10) and not the bound behind (x >= 0 needs y <= 5). With the row deleted and x = 5 - y substituted the reduced model is min -5 - 2 y over y in [0, 10]: optimum -25 at y = 10, which postsolves to x = -5. By enumeration: the wrong engine fs_ahead, which is that variant, fails the exact oracle on 902 and the structure check on 1,026 of 1,440,000 campaign models and 26 unit tests; my probe on the model above gives nothing with the right engine and the point (-5, 10) with a bound violation of 5 and the objective -25 with the wrong one. A valid form exists (the column leaves, the row stays as a bound on the other columns), but that is another reduction with its own record and removes no row. The contract in gpu_presolve/include/gprs/rules.hpp:566-571 now says why there is no option, with the model.

switches.choice: The zero-cost singleton rule [R3] takes continuous columns only, only rows with two finite sides, and only when another free entry stays in the row.
switches.option: Two finite sides: options_t::zero_cost_one_sided, default false, other value true, flag --zero-cost-one-sided. Another free entry stays: options_t::zero_cost_whole_row, default false, other value true, flag --zero-cost-whole-row. Continuous columns only: not built.
switches.validity: One finite side: the projection is the same. For L <= a x + g the values g for which an x inside its bounds exists are those with g >= L - (largest a x); the infinite side stays infinite, and the saved row of the interval record has one finite side, which the undo and the checks accept only with the option. Whole row: the row is left without a free entry and with the sides that the terms of its fixed columns must meet for values of the removed columns to exist; the row rules then delete it or report infeasible, which is the truth about the model. Integer columns: lifting the restriction as it stands is not valid, the set of values of the rest has holes. Model: 2 x + y = 1 with x integer in [0, 1] without cost and y in [-1, 1]; only y = -1 and y = 1 have an x, but the rule for continuous columns would leave -1 <= y <= 1. The valid extension (the row is integral for the column, the new sides rounded onto the grid, an undo that steps on integers, interval records with integer columns in the stack contract and in both checks) is a new mechanism and not a switch; amendment F.8 names it as not required.
switches.covered_by: Unit tests switches_zero_cost_one_sided, switches_zero_cost_one_sided_undo, switches_zero_cost_whole_row; the generated-model test takes both on half of its seeds. Campaign: zero_cost_one_sided release 915,276 alone, 7,814 changed; assertion 452,892 / 3,799. zero_cost_whole_row release 907,104 / 517; assertion 452,952 / 270. Wrong engines sw_one_sided_undo (campaign with --switches: oracle 704, structure 719 of 1,440,000; 3 unit tests) and sw_whole_row (oracle 13, structure 13; 1 unit test). Structure check on the 240 and structure and crush check on the 17 pass for both values, also in primal-only mode with the projections (24,465 interval records there with one-sided rows).

With one-sided rows the record stack differs on two instances: on triptim1 the 4 forcing columns leave as 4 interval records, on seymour1 there is one interval record more. No row made only of such columns is met (counter zero_cost_whole_row is 0). Primal-only mode with the projections: one-sided rows give 1.0004 / 1.0005 / 1.0008 over 237; 12 instances change, none larger: neos-4300652-rahue 176,491 / 73,458 / 29,488 to 173,033 / 71,729 / 27,759; map10 and map16715-04 180,619 / 84,932 / 46,053 to 175,791 / 82,763 / 43,878; beasleyC3 4,126 / 1,512 / 2,262 to 4,052 / 1,475 / 2,225; cmflsp50-24-8-8 16,392 to 16,178 columns; supportcase12 27,666 to 27,466 rows. unitcal_7 then ends on the round limit (20 rounds instead of 5) and loses its fixed-point flag (232 flags against 233); rounds in sum 727 against 681. m1_a over engine 0.9561 / 0.9626 / 0.9416 against 0.9557 / 0.9621 / 0.9408. Whole rows: 0 of 240 change. Integer columns (not built): 66,676 zero-cost integer singleton columns in rows with two finite sides are left on 35 instances (the figure of the worth report), and 50,771 of them on 23 instances stand in a row that is integral for them by its ratios (rail02 9,292, neos-3004026-krka 8,580, rail01 8,272, bab6 8,268, highschool1-aigio 7,529). This is the count that AS-029 asks for, and it is not zero. What taking them would gain in size was not measured; a column would leave and its row would stay.

switches.choice: A visit tries the free singleton column first, in increasing column index, then the zero-cost singleton columns; a call serves its lists until they stay empty.
switches.option: options_t::singleton_order, default singleton_order_t::smallest_index (as today), other values largest_pivot, zero_cost_first, single_pass; tool flag --singleton-order <index|largest-pivot|zero-cost-first|single-pass>.
switches.validity: Every reduction is tested on the state as it is when it is applied, so every order gives a right result; the reduced models can differ. zero_cost_first ends the visit after the projection, because the scan of the row is stale then; the row is listed again by its own change. single_pass ends a call after the first pass over the lists that makes a reduction; a presolve that the round limit ends with a list left is no fixed point. A pass without a reduction is followed by another one in the same call, because such a pass can still list columns (list_columns); without that a call could end with a list and without a finding, which the engine reads as a fixed point. That was the state I took over; the test switches_order_single_pass_without_a_reduction fails with it.
switches.covered_by: Unit tests switches_order_largest_pivot, switches_order_zero_cost_first, switches_order_single_pass, switches_order_single_pass_without_a_reduction. Campaign: order_largest_pivot release 913,800 alone, 0 changed; assertion 458,220 / 0: the campaign does not reach this value (generated models never have two singleton columns of one row that both pass). order_zero_cost_first release 913,296 / 3,735; assertion 453,864 / 1,842. order_single_pass release 912,528 / 90; assertion 458,364 / 63. Wrong engines sw_largest_pivot (unit test only), sw_order_stale (the campaign with --switches ends with a crash, and 1 unit test), sw_single_lost (the second presolve of the campaign changes 8 fixed points with --switches, and 1 unit test). Structure and crush checks pass for the three values.

Four of the five are larger in nonzeros and rows. m1_a over engine 0.9540 / 0.9621 / 0.9413 against 0.9557 / 0.9621 / 0.9408. single_pass: one instance changes in each mode, snp-02-004-104: default mode 354,940 / 77,337 / 174,980 to 355,027 / 77,368 / 175,008, primal-only mode 355,046 / 77,357 / 175,101 to 355,118 / 77,383 / 175,119; it ends on the round limit (20 rounds), is larger and loses its fixed-point flag (233 against 234, and 232 against 233); rounds in sum 731 against 707.

switches.choice: The undo of an interval record starts every column at its lower bound (else the upper, else 0) and moves the columns in increasing index.
switches.option: options_t::interval_start, default interval_start_t::lower, other values upper, nearest_zero, middle; flag --interval-start <lower|upper|nearest-zero|middle>. options_t::interval_order, default ascending, other value descending; flag --interval-order <ascending|descending>; the engine writes it to postsolve_t::interval_descending.
switches.validity: Every start value inside the bounds is right: the undo moves the columns from there until the row holds and reaches every value that the bounds allow. The start value is finite and inside the bounds for each setting (the midpoint 0.5 l + 0.5 u cannot round out of [l, u]); the rule already leaves out a column whose term at a finite bound is beyond the size of a readable side, so no start value brings a huge term. Either order fills what the row misses. The column that ends between its start and its bound still gets the quotient of the row, not start plus a step.
switches.covered_by: Unit tests switches_interval_start_and_order, switches_interval_order_with_two_coefficients (new; both orders, from below and from above, with coefficients 1 and 2), switches_undo_choices_reach_the_stack. Campaign: interval_start_upper release 905,520 alone, 1,826 changed; nearest_zero 914,712 / 1,952; middle 910,872 / 1,808; assertion 453,756 / 871, 454,416 / 917, 456,684 / 920. interval_order_descending release 910,164 / 0; assertion 456,168 / 0: the campaign does not reach it, because generated models never give an interval record with two columns. Wrong engines sw_start_outside (campaign with --switches: oracle 10, structure 184; 1 unit test) and sw_descending_coefficient (caught by the new unit test only; before that test no check caught it). The structure check replays the undo with the order of the stack.
switches.measured: 240 local dumps: no value changes a reduced model, by construction (0 of 240 in default mode and in primal-only mode with the projections); only the start values in the records and the postsolved points differ. For each of the four values the structure check on the 240 passes (17,901 interval records, every snapshot tested) and the structure and crush check with points on the 17 passes, including the 336 interval columns of unitcal_7.

switches.choice: The value of an integer forcing column counts as an integer when it lies within 8 rounding units of the terms it was computed from of one.
switches.option: options_t::forcing_rounding_units, default 8 (the literal of before), any value from 0 to tol.side_error / rounding_unit (90 with the defaults); flag --forcing-rounding-units <x>; the engine writes it to postsolve_t::forcing_rounding_units. Measured: 0 and 64.
switches.validity: With 0 the value is rounded into the row as it was computed: always inside the row, and possibly one unit short of what the exact value allows. A larger band can take the value past its row by that many rounding units of the terms; the range keeps band times rounding unit within tol.side_error, the relative rounding that a readable side may carry, so the row stays within the tolerance. choices_in_range tests the range (an assertion in presolve() and in the family, a usage error in the tools).
switches.covered_by: Unit tests switches_forcing_rounding_units and switches_ranges_of_the_choices. Campaign: forcing_rounding_units_0 release 906,732 alone, 18 changed; assertion 456,840 / 6. forcing_rounding_units_64 release 904,860 / 0; assertion 454,452 / 0: the campaign does not reach a value that 64 treats otherwise than 8. Wrong engine sw_band_units (the band in thousandths): structure check 4 without --switches, oracle 211 and structure 205 with it, of 1,440,000 each, and 2 unit tests. The structure check follows the band of the stack: with a band other than 8 the two computations can give neighbouring integers, and the value of postsolve() then stands if the sum lies within the band of the integer between them.
switches.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 of 240 reduced models change with 0 or with 64, in default mode and in primal-only mode with the projections (the option acts in the undo only). switches.choice: A bound of a free singleton column counts as implied by its row within a band of about 2e-7 (implied_tolerance).
switches.option: options_t::implied_band_scale, default 1, a factor on the band from 1 to 1 / (2 * tol.activity_error_share), which is 5 with the defaults; flag --implied-band-scale <x>. Measured: 2 and 5. A factor below 1 (rounding only) is not built.
switches.validity: The restored value can pass its bound by the band, so the range keeps the band within the feasibility tolerance (at 5 it is the tolerance plus rounding). The factor 1000 that the worth reviewer tried is outside the range; the wrong engine fs_band with a band of 1e-3 fails the oracle. Below 1 the option would not loosen anything, but the band is what two candidates of one bound can differ by: a narrower one lets a bound that is the candidate of the row itself fail the test in one presolve and pass it in the next, so the result would no longer be a function of the state alone. That needs a fresh sum in every test, a new mechanism.

switches.choice: The singleton-column rules read a side, a side less the fixed terms, a new side and the term of a zero-cost column at a bound only up to 1e8 in size.
switches.option: options_t::side_guard_scale, default 1, a factor on that size from 1e-3 to 11 with the defaults; flag --side-guard-scale <x>. Measured: 0.01, 2 and 8. Guards off is not built.
switches.validity: The guard keeps the rounding of the operations on a side below the tolerance. With the factor, a rounding unit of the largest side read is the factor times 1.1e-8, and the range leaves room for eight of them inside tol.side_error, so the row stays within the tolerance. The lower end of the range keeps a side of 1e5 readable, which the state needs for a fixed point (fixed terms leave a row without an event up to that size). Off is not valid: a side that holds an absorbed term of 1e20 would be read as if it still held its own value.

assumptions.title: Range of forcing_rounding_units
assumptions.statement: The band of an integer forcing column may be 0 to tol.side_error / rounding_unit rounding units (90 with the defaults). The upper end is my bound for when a value taken past its row still stays within the tolerance on a readable side.
assumptions.alternatives: A band in units of the feasibility tolerance; no upper end
assumptions.measured: 0 and 64 change no reduced model on the 240; 64 never changed a campaign result

assumptions.title: Range of implied_band_scale
assumptions.statement: The factor on the implied-bound band is at least 1 and at most 1 / (2 * tol.activity_error_share), 5 with the defaults, so that the band stays within the feasibility tolerance. Below 1 is refused because the result would stop being a function of the state alone.
assumptions.alternatives: Rounding only (needs a fresh sum per test); a wider band (not valid at 1000)
assumptions.measured: 2 and 5: 0 of 240 change; without a band (scratch binary): 1 of 240 changes, rocII-5-11 by 4 columns

assumptions.title: Range of side_guard_scale
assumptions.statement: The factor on the size of a readable side is at least 1e-3 and at most 11 with the defaults: the upper end leaves room for eight rounding units of the largest side inside tol.side_error, the lower end keeps a side of 1e5 readable.
assumptions.alternatives: Guards off (not valid); a limit relative to the row
assumptions.measured: 0.01, 2, 8: 0 of 240 change; the guards refuse nothing on the 240

assumptions.title: When a single-pass call ends
assumptions.statement: With singleton_order single_pass a call ends after the first pass that makes a reduction, not after the first pass. A pass without a reduction is followed by another, because it can list columns.
assumptions.alternatives: End after any pass and report the call as stopped
assumptions.measured: The test switches_order_single_pass_without_a_reduction fails with the other form; on the 240 the result equals the first agent's run (one instance, snp-02-004-104)

assumptions.title: Details of the other orders
assumptions.statement: largest_pivot breaks a tie of equal coefficients by the smaller index. zero_cost_first ends the visit when the zero-cost columns left and goes on with the free singleton column otherwise.
assumptions.alternatives: The smallest growth ratio including the history factor; a rescan of the row in the same visit
assumptions.measured: largest_pivot changes 0 of 240; zero_cost_first changes 5 instances in primal-only mode with the projections

assumptions.title: What the growth forms leave as it is
assumptions.statement: In every form of growth_ratio the factor that a substitution passes to the columns of its saved row is computed over the whole row, and column_stats_t::max_growth is taken over the ratios that the form read (0 for an exempt integer pivot).
assumptions.alternatives: Pass the factor on over continuous columns only
assumptions.measured: Not measured apart: the history factor refuses 0 columns on the 240 in every form

assumptions.title: What a counter counts
assumptions.statement: A column that is tried and stays counts once per visit, at the first test that fails, in the order of the tests. refused_ahead or refused_behind is decided from the state as it is, without a fresh sum (an end that would need one counts as not implied). zero_cost_integer_integral asks for exact integer ratios and all other free columns integer, not for the side. A cost counts as small up to 1e-7 and a moved cost as nearly cancelled within 1e-9; both constants decide no reduction. rows_visited and pivots_tried are sums of other counters, taken at the end of a call.
assumptions.alternatives: Count columns once per presolve; count with the tolerances of integral_for
assumptions.measured: All sums that the M1 worth report has are reproduced exactly

assumptions.title: What --left measures
assumptions.statement: The columns that are left are counted by presolving the reduced model once more with the same options and max_rounds 1, and reading the counters of that one call of the family. It is a tool step after the report of the first presolve is complete, so it costs the engine nothing.
assumptions.alternatives: A statistic computed inside the engine after the last round
assumptions.measured: 375,627 columns in 317,741 rows on 126 of the 240, the figures of the worth report; the first result is unchanged by the flag (0 differences on the 240)

assumptions.title: How the campaign draws the options
assumptions.statement: With --switches six seeds in ten get one other value, three get each of the 20 values with probability 0.3, one keeps the defaults. The values come from a random stream seeded by the seed alone that nothing else reads. A result counts as changed when status, hash of the reduced model, hash of the stack, or the postsolved images of two points of the reduced model differ from the presolve without the drawn values.
assumptions.alternatives: Other shares; more values per option
assumptions.measured: Per value about 3% of the models have it alone and 9% among several; five values never changed a result

assumptions.title: The structure check with a band other than 8
assumptions.statement: When the stack carries a forcing band other than 8 rounding units and the check's own undo gives the neighbouring integer, the value of postsolve() stands if the sum lies within the band of the integer between them; the rows and bounds are then tested with it. At the default band the two must agree as before.

I could not make it happen again (four reruns of the part, one rerun of the whole run, the seed alone in both builds, a probe of the model with and without the drawn option) and the point it prints is feasible for the model it prints. A value of 2 where the true value is 0 is one flipped bit of a double, so I think it was a fault of the machine during that check, but I cannot prove that. The first agent's run of the same seeds on almost the same source had no failure either. If it is a real defect, it is rarer than one in 45 million models and the sanitizer samples did not see it.

Time. The two runs give +0.7% and +0.2% on a machine that other agents kept busy; two copies of one binary differ by 0.2%. The counting costs the family about 9%, which I could not bring lower without removing counters that the task asks for.

The validity of the two narrower growth forms rests on postsolve() rounding the integer columns of the reduced point before any undo. A caller that postsolves a point with integer columns far from integers gets no guard from the limit for those columns in these forms.

side_guard_scale above 1 and implied_band_scale above 1 let the engine work closer to the tolerance. The ranges are argued in the header; on the 240 and in the campaign they change almost nothing, so they are tested by unit tests only.
